---
title: "Task 1: Does including headings improve classification?"
author: "Jacob Low"
output: pdf_document
---

## Objective

Compare binary classification accuracy using paragraph text alone
versus paragraph text plus HTML headings.

## Setup

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(textrecipes)

source("../scripts/preprocessing.R")
load("../data/claims-raw.RData")
```

## Extract text

```{r extract}
paragraphs_only <- parse_data(claims_raw)
with_headers <- parse_data(claims_raw, include_headers = TRUE)

stopifnot(identical(paragraphs_only$.id, with_headers$.id))
```

## Split data into training and test sets

```{r split}
set.seed(200)
split <- initial_split(
  paragraphs_only,
  prop = 0.8,
  strata = bclass
)

train_paragraphs <- training(split)
test_paragraphs <- testing(split)

train_headers <- with_headers %>%
  filter(.id %in% train_paragraphs$.id)

test_headers <- with_headers %>%
  filter(.id %in% test_paragraphs$.id)
```

## Paragraph only

```{r paragraph-only}

paragraph_recipe <- recipe(
  bclass ~ text_clean,
  data = train_paragraphs
) %>%
  step_tokenize(text_clean) %>%
  step_stopwords(text_clean) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(text_clean, max_tokens = 1000) %>%
  step_tfidf(text_clean) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(), num_comp = tune())
```

## logistic regression setup

```{r logistic-regression-setup}
paragraph_model <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm") %>%
  set_mode("classification")
paragraph_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(paragraph_recipe) %>%
  add_model(paragraph_model)
```


## cross validation

```{r cross-validation}
set.seed(200)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_paragraphs, v = 5, strata = bclass)

component_grid <- tibble(
  num_comp = c(5L, 10L, 20L, 40L)
)

paragraph_cv <- tune_grid(
  paragraph_workflow,
  resamples = cv_folds,
  grid = component_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(accuracy)
)

collect_metrics(paragraph_cv)
```

Results of this show that 40 components has the greatest accuracy. We run with more components to see where improvement levels off.

```{r}
component_grid <- tibble(
  num_comp = c(40L, 60L, 80L, 100L)
)

paragraph_cv <- tune_grid(
  paragraph_workflow,
  resamples = cv_folds,
  grid = component_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(accuracy)
)

collect_metrics(paragraph_cv)
```

80 components seems to have performed the best among the tested values.

```{r}
best_paragraph <- select_best(
  paragraph_cv,
  metric = "accuracy"
)

best_paragraph
final_paragraph_workflow <- finalize_workflow(
  paragraph_workflow,
  best_paragraph
)

paragraph_fit <- fit(
  final_paragraph_workflow,
  data = train_paragraphs
)
```

## including header

```{r including-header}
header_recipe <- recipe(
  bclass ~ text_clean,
  data = train_headers
) %>%
  step_tokenize(text_clean) %>%
  step_stopwords(text_clean) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(text_clean, max_tokens = 1000) %>%
  step_tfidf(text_clean) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(), num_comp = tune())

header_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(header_recipe) %>%
  add_model(paragraph_model)

```

## assigning same cv splits as training
```{r assigning-same-cv-splits}
header_splits <- purrr::map(cv_folds$splits, function(s) {

  train_rows <- match(
    analysis(s)$.id,
    train_headers$.id
  )

  validation_rows <- match(
    assessment(s)$.id,
    train_headers$.id
  )

  stopifnot(!anyNA(train_rows), !anyNA(validation_rows))

  make_splits(
    list(
      analysis = train_rows,
      assessment = validation_rows
    ),
    data = train_headers
  )
})

header_folds <- manual_rset(
  splits = header_splits,
  ids = cv_folds$id
)
```

## component testing for headers to find the best tuned model for headers
```{r component-testing-for-headers}
header_grid <- tibble(
  num_comp = c(5L, 10L, 20L, 40L, 60L, 80L, 100L)
)

set.seed(200)

header_cv <- tune_grid(
  header_workflow,
  resamples = header_folds,
  grid = header_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(accuracy)
)

collect_metrics(header_cv)
```

Our results show that the best tuned model for headers uses 80 components.

```{r selecting-best-header-model}
best_header <- select_best(header_cv, metric = "accuracy")

header_fit <- header_workflow %>%
  finalize_workflow(best_header) %>%
  fit(data = train_headers)
```

## evaluating both models
```{r evaluating-both-models}
paragraph_test_predictions <- predict(
  paragraph_fit,
  new_data = test_paragraphs
) %>%
  bind_cols(test_paragraphs %>% select(.id, bclass))

header_test_predictions <- predict(
  header_fit,
  new_data = test_headers
) %>%
  bind_cols(test_headers %>% select(.id, bclass))
  bind_rows(
  accuracy(
    paragraph_test_predictions,
    truth = bclass,
    estimate = .pred_class
  ) %>% mutate(version = "Paragraphs only"),

  accuracy(
    header_test_predictions,
    truth = bclass,
    estimate = .pred_class
  ) %>% mutate(version = "Paragraphs + headings")
) %>%
  select(version, .metric, .estimate)
```
